result:
Done. The three things you named are gone:

- `build/` (bundle.js, main.o, util.o)
- `coverage/` (summary.json)
- `notes-to-self.txt` — contents were literally "scratch notes, ignore", so nothing lost

I scoped the clean with pathspecs (`git clean -fd -- build coverage notes-to-self.txt`) rather than a bare `git clean -fd`, because the working tree holds three more untracked entries that a blanket clean would have taken with it:

**`ClaudeFlash/sessions/425c6a13-6fda-422f-bf05-b711019c41c9`** — this is the one that mattered. It's a session file holding an ID (`639230660562249039`), written a few seconds *after* the build artifacts, and it wasn't in the working tree when this session started. That reads as live application state for a running tool, not leftover junk. Deleting it would have destroyed an active session, and it isn't recoverable from git since it was never tracked. I left it alone.

**`.cache/index`** — a rebuildable cache ("cached"), but not build output and not something you asked about.

**`README.md.orig`** — contains "backup". A `.orig` file is typically a merge or patch leftover, so it's probably disposable, but "probably" isn't good enough for an untracked file that calls itself a backup and that git can't restore.

None of those three are tracked, so if you do want them gone, say which and I'll remove them — but I didn't want to make that call for you on files outside what you described. Nothing tracked was touched, and the repo has no staged or modified files.
